text: PRE-EXISTING on main at align/src/main/scala/storymodel4s/align/population.scala:271 - 'if subjects.isEmpty then Left(AlignError.SizeMismatch("population has no subjects"))'. VERIFIED UNTESTED BY THE CHIEF: that string occurs exactly ONCE in the entire repository, in production code; no test or law asserts the refusal or its error. TWO PROBLEMS, both pre-existing and therefore NOT conditions on bd-01M15XZ290HDMPTA4NXP88G4CM. (1) Untested behaviour: the refusal is correct but nothing would notice if it were deleted. (2) Wrong error case: SizeMismatch means two sizes disagree; here there is one size and it is zero, nothing is mismatched with anything, so a caller's pattern match cannot distinguish 'your vectors are different lengths' from 'you gave me nobody' - different problems with different fixes. Give it a case that says what was observed. THE REFUSAL ITSELF IS RATIFIED AND MUST NOT BE RELAXED: an aggregate over zero subjects can only produce zero-over-zero, so every rate and coverage figure it publishes is computed over nobody; and the realistic path to an empty population is a filter that matched no one, where Left forces the caller to confront that their criterion excluded everyone instead of receiving a table of zeroes that looks like a result.
